references.text: God places fear and dread upon the nations, just as in Exodus 15:16 where 'אֵימָתָה וָפַחַד' (dread and fear) falls upon the enemies.
The Lord's promise to place fear and dread upon all peoples who hear about Israel, parallel to the fear that fell upon the Canaanites.
Rahab describes how fear fell over the inhabitants of Jericho when they heard about Israel's departure from Egypt and the crossing of the Red Sea.
Reference to the people God has 'קָנִיתָ' (bought/acquired), the same expression used for Israel in Exodus 15:16.
Describes how God led His people to His holy land which He had acquired with His right hand, parallel to 'עַם־זוּ קָנִיתָ'.
God's mighty arm ('זְרוֹעֲ') that crushes enemies, parallel to 'בִּגְדֹל זְרוֹעֲךָ' in Exodus 15:16.
Reference to the Lord's arm that acted at the departure from Egypt and the crossing through the sea.
God's promise to deliver Israel with an outstretched arm, the same theme of God's mighty arm as in the song of victory.
Paul speaks of the church which God has 'won for Himself' (περιεποιήσατο), parallel to 'עַם־זוּ קָנִיתָ' - the people God has bought.
Believers are called 'a people for His own possession' (λαὸς εἰς περιποίησιν), reflecting the idea of Israel as God's acquired people.
God inflicts dread upon the enemy as a tool to protect His people and reveal their human weakness.
God's raised hand/arm first creates fear in the enemy, before ending with their shame and destruction.
Both verses show how God uses dread as a strategic weapon to neutralize the enemy's threat against His people.
Deuteronomy interprets and applies the event in Exodus 15 as an eternal pattern for God's salvation through fear in the enemy.
Both verses illustrate how God creates unreasonable fear in the enemy that leads to their total collapse.
Complementary descriptions of the same event: God's wrath consumes the enemies while fear paralyzes them to secure Israel's passage.
